description: Adjust tunable file system parameters on an ext2/ext3/ext4 file system.

option.name: -c
tip: Set the number of mounts after which e2fsck checks the file system.
Use random, 0 or -1 for the documented special cases.

option.name: -C
tip: Set the number of times the file system has been mounted.

option.name: -e
tip: Set the kernel behavior when errors are detected.
Possible values: continue, remount-ro, panic

option.name: -E
tip: Set comma-separated extended options.
See tune2fs(8) for the supported options.

option.name: -f
tip: Force the operation even when errors are encountered.

option.name: -g
tip: Set the group that may use the reserved blocks.
Accepts a group name or numeric gid.

option.name: -i
tip: Set the maximum time between two file system checks.
Use a d, m or w suffix; 0 disables the check.

option.name: -I
tip: Change the inode size used by the file system.

option.name: -j
tip: Add an ext3 journal to the file system.

option.name: -J
tip: Set comma-separated journal options.
See tune2fs(8) for the supported options.

option.name: -l
tip: List the contents of the file system superblock.

option.name: -L
tip: Set the volume label, up to 16 characters.

option.name: -m
tip: Set the percentage of blocks reserved for privileged processes.

option.name: -M
tip: Set the last-mounted directory.

option.name: -o
tip: Set or clear default mount options.
Prefix an option with ^ to clear it.

option.name: -O
tip: Set or clear file system features.
Prefix a feature with ^ to clear it.

option.name: -Q
tip: Set quota options and the quota feature.
Possible values: usrquota, grpquota, prjquota
Prefix an option with ^ to clear it.

option.name: -r
tip: Set the number of reserved file system blocks.

option.name: -T
tip: Set the time the file system was last checked.
Use now or a date understood by the system.

option.name: -u
tip: Set the user who may use the reserved blocks.
Accepts a user name or numeric uid.

option.name: -U
tip: Set the file system UUID.
Possible values: clear, random, time
Any explicit UUID is also accepted.

option.name: -z
tip: Write the old contents of each block to an undo file.
